en: Puxian Pusa Xingyuan Zan (Hymn to the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva).
Kai fu yi tong san si te jin shi hong lu qing su guo gong shi yi san qian hu ci zi zeng si kong (Grand Master of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Su with a Fief of Three Thousand Households, Invested with Purple Robes, Posthumously Honored as Minister of Works).
To all the lions among men throughout the worlds of the ten directions, and to all those who have appeared in the three periods of time,
I now pay homage without exception, with body, speech, and mind entirely pure.
With bodies as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields, I pay homage to all Tathāgatas;
with my mind directed toward every Buddha, I do so through the power of these practices and vows of Samantabhadra.
Upon the tip of a single atom are Buddhas as numerous as atoms, with all the Buddhas and their sons seated therein;
thus throughout the entire dharma-realm without exception, I believe that all the Buddhas completely fill it.
Within that inexhaustible ocean of merit, when I proclaim the virtues of the Tathāgata through an ocean of melodic sounds, I shall ever praise all the Sugatas.
With supreme flower garlands and fragrant ointments, And with music, excellent parasols,
and all manner of most exquisite ornaments, I make offerings to all the Tathāgatas.
With supreme garments and various incenses, with heaps of powdered incense as vast as Mount Sumeru,
and with extraordinary lamps and burning incense, I make offerings to all the Tathāgatas;
all unsurpassed and expansive offerings, I fully resolve upon for all the Tathāgatas.
By the power of my resolute conviction in the practices of Samantabhadra, I pay homage to and make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
Whatever sinful karma I have previously committed— all arising from greed, hatred, and delusion,
and likewise through body, speech, and mind— I confess it all before them all.
Whatever merit all sentient beings throughout the ten directions possess— whether those in training, those beyond training, pratyekabuddhas,
as well as the sons of the Buddha and all Tathāgatas— I rejoice in it all with my whole being.
All the lamps of the worlds throughout the ten directions, Who have realized bodhi and attained freedom from defilement—
I now entreat all those World-Honored Ones To turn the unsurpassed, wondrous wheel of Dharma.
To all those who intend to manifest parinirvāṇa, I join my palms and entreat them:
may you remain for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of all living beings.
I prostrate, make offerings, and confess my transgressions; I rejoice in merit, and entreat [the Buddhas to remain].
Whatever roots of virtue I have accumulated, I dedicate them all toward awakening.
As I train myself in the teachings of all Tathāgatas, And bring to perfection the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra,
May I make offerings to all Buddhas of the past, And to all those currently dwelling throughout the ten directions;
May I swiftly accomplish all that is yet to come in the future, Fulfilling my aspirations and realizing supreme enlightenment.
May all the lands throughout the ten directions Be vast and entirely pure;
May all Buddhas proceed to the King of Bodhi Trees, And may the sons of the Buddhas fill them all;
May all sentient beings throughout the ten directions Attain peace and happiness, free from all afflictions.
May all living beings obtain the benefit of the Dharma, And may their wishes be fulfilled according to their hearts' desire.
When I practice for the sake of Bodhi, May I remember my past lives throughout all realms of existence;
Whether undergoing birth and death within various births, May I always choose to leave the household life.
Their conduct of precepts is stainless and ever-pure; they always practice without deficiency or flaw.
Whether in the languages of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, or humans—in the tongues of all living beings—they preach the Dharma through every possible sound.
Constantly practicing the sublime pāramitās, they do not become deluded regarding the mind of enlightenment.
All their sins and obstacles are completely extinguished without remainder;
they attain liberation from karma, afflictions, and the realms of Māra within the paths of the world.
Just as a lotus flower is unsullied by water, And as the sun and moon are unsullied by the sky;
May the sufferings of all evil realms be stilled, And may all living beings be brought to peace and happiness;
May I act for the benefit of all sentient beings, Throughout all the lands of the ten directions.
Constantly practicing in accordance with all sentient beings, may I bring the sublime conduct of Bodhi to fulfillment.
May I cultivate the practices and vows of Samantabhadra;
throughout future kalpas, as I practice, may I always gather together with all those who share the same path as me.
In the actions of body, speech, and mind, may I practice with a single resolve and vow;
may all spiritual friends who benefit me manifest for me the conduct of Samantabhadra;
may I always gather together with them, and toward them all, may I never feel weariness.
May I always behold the faces of all Tathāgatas, surrounded by the sons of the Buddhas;
may I offer vast offerings to them all, never growing weary throughout all future kalpas.
Constantly upholding the subtle and wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas, May they cause all practices for enlightenment to shine forth,
And may they purify all practices of Samantabhadra, Cultivating them throughout all future kalpas.
While wandering through the various realms of existence, may their merit and wisdom be inexhaustible;
through prajñā, skillful means, meditative concentration, and liberation, may they attain an inexhaustible treasury of merit.
As within a single atom there are lands as numerous as atoms, Within those Buddha-lands, inconceivable Buddhas and their heirs sit;
They constantly behold the supreme and wondrous conduct of Bodhi.
In this way, throughout all infinite directions, within the measure of a single hair-tip across the three periods of time,
may I enter and practice through oceans of Buddhas, oceans of lands, and oceans of eons.

Within the ocean of merit of a single sound, they always gain entry into the eloquence of the Buddhas— the pure voices of all Tathāgatas and the sounds corresponding to the inclinations of all sentient beings.
Within that inexhaustible sound, when all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time turn the sublime wheel of the principle,
may I, through the power of my wisdom, be able to enter it universally.
In a single kṣaṇa, I enter all future moments;
I enter all kalpas of the future, and all the infinite kalpas of the three times, entering koṭis of kalpas within a single kṣaṇa.
All the Lions among Men of the three periods of time, I behold them all in a single instant;
I constantly enter their spheres of activity through the power of liberation that is like an illusion.
All the wondrously adorned lands of the three periods of time can be manifested within the tip of a single atom;
thus, throughout all such infinite directions and locations, one is able to enter the adorned buddha-fields of all Buddhas.
All those lamps of the world in future ages, Who shall all awaken and turn the wheel of Dharma,
And manifest final nirvāṇa in ultimate stillness— To all those World-Honored Ones, I shall go.
With the power of supernormal feats, universally swift; with the power of the vehicle, pervading all gateways;
with the power of conduct, equal in merit; with the power of loving-kindness, pervading all actions;
with the power of merit, universally sublime; with the power of wisdom, acting without attachment.
Through the power of prajñā, skillful means, and meditative concentration, and by accumulating the majestic power of bodhi,
may all be purified through the power of karma. Now I shall destroy the power of afflictions and completely subdue the power of Māra, fulfilling all the powers of Samantabhadra.
Universally purifying oceans of buddha-fields, Universally liberating oceans of sentient beings,
Able to thoroughly observe oceans of all phenomena, And attaining their source within the ocean of wisdom;
Universally causing the oceans of conduct to be entirely pure, And further causing the oceans of vows to be fully perfected.
I shall offer worship to all the oceans of Buddha-assemblies, And practice the conduct of Samantabhadra without weariness throughout kalpas.
May I fulfill, without exception, all the various distinctions Of the bodhi-conduct and vows of all Tathāgatas of the three times,
And awaken to bodhi through the conduct of Samantabhadra.
The Tathāgatas, the Buddhas, have an eldest son, Whose name is proclaimed as the Honored One Samantabhadra;
All, through that wisdom, accord with wondrous conduct, Dedicating all roots of goodness to every being.
May my actions of body, speech, and mind be pure; may all my practices be pure and my buddha-field be pure.
Just as he whose name is Samantabhadra possesses such wisdom, may I now become entirely equal to him.
The conduct and vows of Samantabhadra are universally sublime;
I shall practice the conduct of Mañjuśrī, without weariness throughout all future kalpas, bringing everything to complete perfection without exception.
The sublime practices required are immeasurable, and all their merits are beyond measure;
having abided in these infinite cultivations, they fully know all those supernormal powers.
Even until the ultimate limit of space is reached, and sentient beings are likewise brought to the ultimate end without exception—
Until karma and afflictions are utterly exhausted, even until my vows are likewise all fulfilled.
If there were infinite lands throughout the ten directions, adorned with jewels and offered to all Buddhas,
along with the sublime peace and happiness of gods and humans, and one were to practice such giving for as many eons as there are atoms in those lands.
If a person, upon hearing this Sovereign of Supreme Aspirations even once,
can give rise to a mind of resolute faith and seek with thirsty longing for supreme enlightenment, they shall obtain a preeminent mass of merit surpassing all others.
They shall be far removed from all evil realms, And they shall all be far removed from all evil companions.
Swiftly they shall behold Amitāyus, By recollecting only the supreme vows and conduct of Samantabhadra;
Attaining great benefit and a sublime lifespan, A life well-lived for such a person.
Just as that Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, so shall that person soon obtain [his state].
Whatever karmic offenses of the five immediate transgressions were committed through a lack of wisdom,
when they recite the *Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna*, these shall be swiftly extinguished without remainder.
With wisdom, countenance, and the marks of excellence, Achieving perfection in lineage and kind,
Unassailable by Māras and non-Buddhists, Constantly receiving offerings throughout the three realms,
Swiftly proceeding to the Bodhi tree, And sitting there to benefit sentient beings.
Awakening to Bodhi and turning the wheel of Dharma, Subduing Māra along with his hosts;
If there are those who uphold these vows of Samantabhadra, Reading, reciting, receiving, maintaining, and expounding them— The Tathāgata fully knows the fruits and rewards they shall obtain;
They will attain supreme Bodhi, so do not harbor any doubt.
Just as the heroic wisdom of Mañjuśrī, and likewise the wisdom of Samantabhadra—
when I shall practice and study in that manner, I dedicate all roots of goodness.
All Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, by means of these supreme dedications,
have dedicated all my roots of goodness toward the conduct of Samantabhadra.
When one is about to pass away and relinquish this life, all karmic obstructions shall be transformed;
one will personally behold the Infinite Light and swiftly proceed to that land, the realm of Ultimate Bliss.
May all supreme aspirations for one another be fully realized before me;
may I bring them all to perfection without exception, for the benefit of sentient beings in the world.
Extremely majestic within that Buddha’s assembly, Born from within a most excellent lotus flower,
There he obtained the prophecy of enlightenment; Having personally stood before the Tathāgata Amitābha,
And having received that prophecy there, He manifested billions of infinite emanations.
Extensively performing all manner of benefit and happiness for sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions by the power of wisdom—
should any person recite and uphold the vows of Samantabhadra and accumulate all their roots of goodness,
they shall attain their wishes in a single instant, and by this, all living beings shall obtain supreme vows.
Having attained these practices of Samantabhadra, this supreme and immeasurable mass of merit,
may all sentient beings who are submerged in evil habits proceed to the palace of the Buddha Amitābha.
To the one who can shatter the door-panels of the gate to the palace of parinirvāṇa,
To the one who enjoys the Dharma of all Buddhas, To the Savior of the World, I prostrate.
From his own hand he flows forth clear water, Able to remove the thirst of hungry ghosts.
The wish-fulfilling tree of the three realms, I prostrate to the Lotus-Handed One.
With great compassion as his heart, he is able to extinguish the fire of hatred;
I prostrate to the Honored One Maitreya, who can sever the bowstring of desire.
Gāthā: With the wondrous wisdom of Ākāśagarbha, The Honored One tranquil as space, liberated from the flow of birth and death— I prostrate to the Son of the Buddha’s Heart.
He is able to quell the delusions of boundless sentient beings And the minds that find no benefit.
I prostrate to Samantabhadra, the foremost son of the Sugata;
To him whose afflictions are but servants, who has utterly surpassed the armies of Māra.
I prostrate to Vajrapāṇi, the one capable of expounding all vidyās.
I prostrate to Mañjuśrī, who bears the form of a sublime youth;
who extends the lamp of wisdom everywhere and seizes the light of the three realms.
He is the remover of all veils; therefore, I prostrate to him.
Inexhaustible Honored One of Wisdom, Able to give birth to unfailing eloquence;
Like the earth, the sole support for all sentient beings,
Uninterrupted, treasury of firm wisdom and compassion— To Kṣitigarbha, I prostrate.
This is the true son of the Sugata; may the merit obtained from this praise cause all sentient beings to become worthy vessels for such praise as he.
The Dhāraṇī for the Swift Fulfillment of the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is as follows:

*Śrīmatsidvireśvarīye svāhā oṃ aśvavāravidhi svāhā.* If one recites this mantra immediately after daily reciting the *Samantabhadra-caryā-praṇidhāna*, then upon reciting it even once, all the vows of Samantabhadra’s conduct will be completely fulfilled. For those who practice *samādhi*, the samādhi will swiftly manifest before them; they will obtain the two kinds of adornments—merit and wisdom—and attain the firm Dharma, achieving swift accomplishment.
